newsitem.title: USA: Mobil sees profitable Indonesian natgas growth.
newsitem.headline: Mobil sees profitable Indonesian natgas growth.

text.p: Mobil Corp said Tuesday it sees profitable growth in Indonesia's natural gas market.

The company "is optimistic about its future in Indonesia and Southeast Asia, a region in which energy consumption has risen 300 percent since the 1970s and will double again by 2010," it said in a statement about Chief Executive Officer Lucio A. Noto's speech to the Indonesian Petroleum Association in Jakarta Tuesday.
The statement's headline contained its only reference to expected profits.

"As a major player in the global energy business, you've got to be where the action is. That's why Mobil is here to stay," Noto said, reiterating Mobil's ongoing commitment to energy development in the region.
He also outlined additional steps Indonesia could take to help achieve sustainable growth well into the 21st century energy market.

Mobil noted it has operated the Arun field in North Sumatra since 1978, and said the field currently produces 2.3 billion cubic feet per day of natural gas. Mobil's 1995 net production from the field was 1.5 billion cubic feet daily, with 77,000 barrels per day of condensate.

Mobil is developing the nearby South Lhok Sukon A&D and Pase fields, with initial production scheduled for 1997. Production is also scheduled to begin in 1999 from the NSO "A" field off the northeast coast of Sumatra.

In addition, Mobil said, it has agreed to join Exxon Corp and Indonesian state oil company Pertamina to evaluate the commerciality of producing natural gas from the Natuna field, the largest in Indonesia, with estimated recoverable reserves of 46 trillion cubic feet. -- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.
